title: crafter-station/petdex
claim: crafter-station/petdex — The public gallery of animated pet for Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode y Gemini CLI
why_good: A cute gallery of animated desktop pets for coding-agent terminals — fun and shareable, but pure novelty.
value: No real revenue path beyond maybe cosmetic packs; a delightful side-project, not a company.
risk: Novelty with no moat or retention; the joke fades and platforms can add their own.
pick_reason: The project appears to be a collection of animated pets rather than a distinct product with a clear monetization strategy.

zh.claim: crafter-station/petdex —— 给 Codex、Claude Code、OpenCode、Gemini CLI 的动画宠物公共画廊。
zh.why_good: 给编码 agent 终端的一堆可爱动画桌宠——好玩、易传播,但纯属新奇。
zh.value: 除了也许卖点装饰包,没有真正的收入路径;是个讨喜的业余项目,不是公司。
zh.risk: 新奇无护城河、无留存;梗一过就凉,平台也能自己加。
zh.hook: 给编码 agent 终端的可爱动画桌宠——纯粹好玩,零护城河。
zh.does: 一个公开的动画像素宠物画廊，宠物住在 coding agent 的终端里：3686 星、167 fork，还有一个投稿队列，人们把自己手画的小生物传上去——其中源源不断有中文投稿，还有一位版权方来要求下架。
zh.gap: 宠物被关在终端里，只有程序员看得见。这件事真正更老也更大的受众——桌面宠物、Shimeji 那一脉——待在普通人的电脑和手机上，而他们从 2010 年代起就只能用一批停止维护的免费软件。
zh.counter: 半衰期很短的新鲜感，且没有护城河：梗会过去，握着终端的那一方会自己发一个，而画廊真正的资产——用户投稿的画——在赚到第一分钱之前就已经引来了 IP 下架请求（issue #651）。桌宠还免费了十五年，为它收费是件没被验证过的事。
zh.differentiator: 拿走流水线，扔掉终端。真正有意思的是：普通人正在成规模地画并投稿像素小生物。产品是「画一只，就得到一个会对你此刻在干什么做出反应的动画桌宠」——放在 Windows 和 macOS 上，桌宠受众本来就在那里。冷启动（中文）：小红书、B站搜「桌宠 自制」，以及 Shimeji 教程下的评论区，挤满做到一半放弃的人；冷启动（英文）：r/Shimeji 与 r/desktops。
zh.why_use: 想让屏幕上住一只小东西的人：桌宠受众是中学生和上班族，不是程序员。他拿到的是一只自己画出来、会动的伙伴。
zh.edge: 把一张手画角色变成干净的循环精灵图，过去是画师一下午的活。图生精灵把它压成一次上传——这也是一个公开投稿队列能以这个速度被业余画作塞满的唯一原因。

hook: Cute animated pets for your coding-agent terminal — pure delight, zero moat.

voices.quote: 这两个条目属于同一公开品牌 IP 的历史提交，当前不再属于授权发布集

does: A public gallery of animated sprite pets that live in a coding-agent terminal: 3.7k stars, 167 forks, and a submission queue where people upload their own hand-drawn creatures — including a steady stream of Chinese submissions and one rights-holder asking for a takedown.
gap: The pets are trapped in a terminal, where only programmers see them. The much older and much larger audience for this — the 桌面宠物 tradition, Shimeji, desktop companions — sits on ordinary desktops and phones and has been served by abandoned 2010-era freeware ever since.
counter: Novelty with a short half-life and no moat: the joke fades, whoever owns the terminal ships their own, and the gallery's real asset — user-submitted art — is already producing IP takedown requests (issue #651) before it has produced a cent. Desktop pets have also been free for fifteen years; charging for one is an unproven act.
differentiator: Take the pipeline, drop the terminal. The interesting part is that ordinary people are drawing and submitting sprite creatures at volume; the product is 'draw one pet, get an animated desktop companion that reacts to what you are actually doing' — on Windows and macOS, where the 桌宠 audience already is. Cold start (Chinese): 小红书 and B站 搜「桌宠 自制」and the Shimeji tutorial comment sections, full of people who gave up mid-way; Cold start (English): r/Shimeji and r/desktops.
consumer_angle: Non-developer user: someone who wants company on their screen — the audience that kept Shimeji alive for a decade. Finished thing: their own drawing, animated, living on their desktop.
why_use: Someone who wants a small creature living on their screen: the 桌宠 audience, which is teenagers and office workers, not programmers. What they walk away with is an animated companion drawn in their own hand.
edge: Turning one hand-drawn character into a clean looping sprite sheet used to be an artist's afternoon. Image-to-sprite generation collapsed it to a single upload — which is the only reason a public submission queue is filling with amateur art at this rate at all.
